Since the hash is computed over results in original order, I'll need each rank to compute its portion locally, then gather everything back to rank 0 in the correct order before running the Kahan summation and hash computation exactly as before.\n\nSince option generation is deterministic based on index alone, each rank can generate just its own slice rather than all options, which saves memory and work. I'll time the pricing computation specifically (barrier before, MAX reduce after across ranks) and keep validation and the default option count unchanged.\n\nFor edge cases like numOptions=0, I'll replicate the original's behavior producing NaN in statistics rather than special-casing it. For argument parsing and error handling, all ranks parse identically but only rank 0 prints output, with MPI_Finalize called properly before any exit path; the validation decision stays root-only since only root gathers the full results array.\n\nFor performance, I'm using block distribution across ranks (no input communication needed since each rank generates its own slice), then gathering results to root with MPI_Gatherv—80MB at 10M options is manageable. I'm considering skipping the gather entirely when neither -r nor -v flags are set, since the results vector would otherwise be computed and discarded unused.\n\nI'll simplify by setting the needed count based on whether printing (full N) or just validating (min 10), so root only allocates a results buffer of that size. The root can also write its own local results directly into that buffer instead of going through the gather step, avoiding unnecessary copying.\n\nRather than micro-optimizing with MPI_IN_PLACE offsets, I'll just compute each rank's local results into its own buffer and gather them all, since the memcpy cost is trivial compared to the pricing computation itself.\n\nFor the clipping logic, I need recvcounts and displacements per rank to handle the case where `needed` falls partway through a rank's block — clamping each rank's send count to the overlap with `needed`, and making sure displacements stay valid even when a rank's count is zero.\n\nKeeping option generation outside the timed region matches the original, and timing should only wrap the actual pricing loop — using MPI_Barrier before and MPI_Wtime before/after, then MPI_Reduce with MAX across ranks to get the overall computation time, from which I derive options-per-second exactly as the original does, preserving identical output formatting.\n\nI'm weighing whether to add an informational \"MPI ranks\" line after the validation output — it's useful for understanding scalability but slightly risks breaking anything parsing the output, though I'll include it since it seems low-risk and valuable. I'll stick to plain MPI_Init since thread support isn't needed, and avoid introducing OpenMP since the goal is no new dependencies beyond MPI itself.\n\nFor the per-rank price computation, I want to generate each option on the fly using the global index rather than storing a full array, replicating the exact same floating-point scaling logic (factor based on index, applied to spot and strike) so results stay numerically identical to the original. For validation of the first entries, I can compute the base option value directly via a small helper function without needing the scaled factor, since the check only depends on the index pattern, not the scaling.\n\nI'm also rewriting validateResults to take a function for generating expected options rather than a precomputed vector, keeping the minimum-of-10 check consistent with whatever numOptions is. For reporting, I'll print rank-0-only output, compute throughput as options per second using floating point division, and format timing similarly to the original (milliseconds with three decimals, elapsed time safely handled near zero). Since all options cost about the same to price with no early-exit cases in this test set, I'll just do a straightforward block partition across ranks — giving the first `rem` ranks one extra option each, with start offsets computed accordingly.\n\nSince pricing is embarrassingly parallel, the main communication cost is the gather (only needed with -r/-v) and a single MPI_Reduce otherwise, so scaling should be fine except for inherent per-rank overhead at high rank counts. Results still need to be stored in a local vector per rank so they can be gathered when needed, which also prevents the compiler from optimizing away the computation. I'm keeping the same argument-parsing logic as the original (using atoll for -n, consistent error handling only printed on rank 0), and structuring main to call MPI_Init up front, run the core logic in a separate function, then always call MPI_Finalize before returning so exit codes stay consistent across early-return paths.\n\nFor the build setup, I'll use find_package(MPI REQUIRED) and link against MPI::MPI_CXX, keeping the math library linked too, and keep -march=native as in the original even though it could behave inconsistently across heterogeneous cluster nodes. I'm making sure the project only needs to declare CXX as a language since MPI::MPI_CXX is supported from CMake 3.9+, and verifying everything compiles cleanly under -Wall -Wextra.\n\nSince results_output.hpp is a shared file, I'll avoid modifying it -- the gather operation already preserves ordering so the hash computed from the gathered results should match the original sequential output.\n\nTo verify correctness, I'll copy the entire original source tree to a temp directory outside the workspace, build the unmodified baseline there, and compare its output against my modified version -- this avoids creating any extra files inside the repo itself. {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793116309398,"sessionID":"ses_e81f1bcafffeWKS62Tsv5l1czh","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_017mi5g66LffPV29iBCpMDNp","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/black-scholes_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_mpi_r5/black-scholes/black_scholes.cpp","content":"#include <mpi.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <array>\n#include <climits>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n#ifndef M_PI\n#define M_PI 3.14159265358979323846\n#endif\n#ifndef M_SQRT_2\n#define M_SQRT_2 0.7071067811865475244\n#endif\n#ifndef M_SQRT1_2\n#define M_SQRT1_2 0.7071067811865475244\n#endif\n#ifndef M_1_SQRTPI\n#define M_1_SQRTPI 0.564189583547756286948\n#endif\n\nenum OptionType {\n    CALL = 0,\n    PUT = 1\n};\n\nstruct OptionInput {\n    int type;           // CALL or PUT\n    double strike;      // Strike price\n    double spot;        // Spot price\n    double q;           // Dividend yield\n    double r;           // Risk-free rate\n    double t;           // Time to maturity\n    double vol;         // Volatility\n    double value;       // Expected value (for validation)\n    double tol;         // Tolerance\n};\n\n// Number of leading results checked by validation\ninline constexpr size_t kValidationChecks = 10;\n\n// Contiguous block of the global option index space owned by one rank\nstruct Partition {\n    size_t start;   // first global index\n    size_t count;   // number of options\n};\n\n// Standard normal cumulative distribution function\ninline double cumulativeNormal(const double x) noexcept {\n    return 0.5 * (1.0 + std::erf(x * M_SQRT1_2));\n}\n\n// Standard normal probability density function\ninline double normalPDF(const double x) noexcept {\n    return M_1_SQRTPI * M_SQRT1_2 * exp(-0.5 * x * x);\n}\n\n// Black-Scholes formula for European options\ndouble blackScholes(const OptionInput& option) noexcept {\n    const double S = option.spot;\n    const double K = option.strike;\n    const double r = option.r;\n    const double q = option.q;\n    const double T = option.t;\n    const double sigma = option.vol;\n    \n    if (T <= 0.0 || sigma <= 0.0) {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    \n    const double d1 = (log(S / K) + (r - q + 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T));\n    const double d2 = d1 - sigma * sqrt(T);\n    \n    const double Nd1 = cumulativeNormal(d1);\n    const double Nd2 = cumulativeNormal(d2);\n    const double discount = exp(-r * T);\n    \n    double price;\n    if (option.type == CALL) {\n        price = S * exp(-q * T) * Nd1 - K * discount * Nd2;\n    } else { // PUT\n        price = K * discount * cumulativeNormal(-d2) - S * exp(-q * T) * cumulativeNormal(-d1);\n    }\n    \n    return price;\n}\n\n// Standard test cases for validation\ninline constexpr std::array<OptionInput, 7> getTestOptions() noexcept {\n    return {{\n        {CALL, 40.00, 42.00, 0.04, 0.08, 0.75, 0.35, 5.0975, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 90.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 0.0205, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 100.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 1.8734, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 110.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 9.9413, 1.0e-3},\n        {PUT, 100.00, 90.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 9.9210, 1.0e-3},\n        {PUT, 100.00, 100.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 1.8734, 1.0e-3},\n        {PUT, 100.00, 110.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 0.0408, 1.0e-3},\n    }};\n}\n\n// Option i of the benchmark set. Each option depends only on its global index,\n// so any rank can construct its own slice without communication.\ninline OptionInput makeOption(const size_t i) noexcept {\n    constexpr auto testOptions = getTestOptions();\n\n    // Cycle through test options and vary parameters slightly\n    const OptionInput& base = testOptions[i % testOptions.size()];\n    OptionInput option = base;\n\n    // Add some variation for larger datasets\n    const double factor = 1.0 + 0.1 * (i / static_cast<double>(testOptions.size()));\n    option.spot *= factor;\n    option.strike *= factor;\n    return option;\n}\n\n// Block partition of numOptions across size ranks (first `rem` ranks get one extra)\nPartition blockPartition(const size_t numOptions, const int rank, const int size) noexcept {\n    const size_t p = static_cast<size_t>(size);\n    const size_t r = static_cast<size_t>(rank);\n    const size_t base = numOptions / p;\n    const size_t rem = numOptions % p;\n    return {r * base + std::min(r, rem), base + (r < rem ? 1 : 0)};\n}\n\n// Gather the first numNeeded results (global order) from all ranks onto rank 0.\n// Only meaningful on rank 0 for `results`; other ranks contribute their local part.\nvoid gatherResults(const std::vector<double>& localResults, const size_t numOptions,\n                   const size_t numNeeded, const int rank, const int size,\n                   std::vector<double>& results) {\n    std::vector<int> counts(size);\n    std::vector<int> displs(size);\n    for (int r = 0; r < size; ++r) {\n        const Partition p = blockPartition(numOptions, r, size);\n        const size_t begin = std::min(p.start, numNeeded);\n        const size_t end = std::min(p.start + p.count, numNeeded);\n        counts[r] = static_cast<int>(end - begin);\n        displs[r] = static_cast<int>(begin);\n    }\n\n    if (rank == 0) {\n        results.resize(numNeeded);\n    }\n\n    MPI_Gatherv(localResults.data(), counts[rank], MPI_DOUBLE,\n                rank == 0 ? results.data() : nullptr, counts.data(), displs.data(),\n                MPI_DOUBLE, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n}\n\nbool validateResults(const size_t numOptions, const std::vector<double>& results) {\n    bool allPassed = true;\n    const size_t numChecks = std::min(kValidationChecks, numOptions);\n    \n    printf(\"Checking computed option prices:\\n\");\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numChecks; ++i) {\n        const double computed = results[i];\n        const double expected = makeOption(i).value;\n        const double error = fabs(computed - expected);\n        const double relError = error / (fabs(expected) + 1e-10);\n        \n        printf(\"  Option %zu: computed=%.4f, expected=%.4f, rel_error=%.4e\\n\", \n               i, computed, expected, relError);\n        \n        // Relaxed validation - just check values are positive and reasonable\n        if (computed < 0.0 || computed > 1000.0 || std::isnan(computed) || std::isinf(computed)) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed at option %zu: invalid value %.4f\\n\", i, computed);\n            allPassed = false;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return allPassed;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of options to price (default: 10000)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation against known values\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint runBenchmark(int argc, char** argv, const int rank, const int size) {\n    size_t numOptions = 10000;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments (identical on every rank)\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numOptions = atoll(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            if (rank == 0) {\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            if (rank == 0) {\n                printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    if (rank == 0) {\n        printf(\"Black-Scholes Option Pricing Benchmark\\n\");\n        printf(\"Number of options: %zu\\n\", numOptions);\n        printf(\"MPI ranks: %d\\n\", size);\n        printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    }\n    \n    // Each rank prices its own contiguous block of options\n    const Partition part = blockPartition(numOptions, rank, size);\n    std::vector<double> localResults(part.count);\n    \n    if (rank == 0) {\n        printf(\"Pricing options...\\n\");\n    }\n\n    // Time the parallel pricing phase: all ranks start together, and the\n    // reported time is the slowest rank (the wall-clock time of the phase).\n    MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    const double tStart = MPI_Wtime();\n\n    for (size_t j = 0; j < part.count; ++j) {\n        localResults[j] = blackScholes(makeOption(part.start + j));\n    }\n\n    const double localElapsed = MPI_Wtime() - tStart;\n    double elapsed = 0.0;\n    MPI_Reduce(&localElapsed, &elapsed, 1, MPI_DOUBLE, MPI_MAX, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n\n    if (rank == 0) {\n        printf(\"Computation time: %.3f ms\\n\", elapsed * 1000.0);\n        printf(\"Options per second: %.0f\\n\", numOptions / elapsed);\n    }\n\n    // Only gather what the output actually needs: all results for -r,\n    // the leading results for -v, nothing otherwise.\n    size_t numNeeded = 0;\n    if (printResults) {\n        numNeeded = numOptions;\n    } else if (validate) {\n        numNeeded = std::min(kValidationChecks, numOptions);\n    }\n\n    int exitCode = 0;\n    if (numNeeded > static_cast<size_t>(INT_MAX)) {\n        if (rank == 0) {\n            printf(\"Error: too many results to gather (%zu)\\n\", numNeeded);\n        }\n        return 1;\n    }\n\n    std::vector<double> results;\n    if (numNeeded > 0) {\n        gatherResults(localResults, numOptions, numNeeded, rank, size, results);\n    }\n\n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults && rank == 0) {\n        print_results(results, \"OptionPrices\");\n    }\n    \n    // Validation\n    if (validate && rank == 0) {\n        printf(\"Validating results...\\n\");\n        bool valid = validateResults(numOptions, results);\n        \n        if (valid) {\n            printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n            exitCode = 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    MPI_Bcast(&exitCode, 1, MPI_INT, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    return exitCode;\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);\n\n    int rank = 0;\n    int size = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &size);\n\n    const int exitCode = runBenchmark(argc, argv, rank, size);\n\n    MPI_Finalize();\n    return exitCode;\n}\n"},"output":"Wrote file {"type":"text","timestamp":1793116979974,"sessionID":"ses_e81f1bcafffeWKS62Tsv5l1czh","part":{"id":"prt_17e19b668001xGL3xBdINvoHO7","messageID":"msg_17e19b275001dmceDReWJPvDxR","sessionID":"ses_e81f1bcafffeWKS62Tsv5l1czh","type":"text","text":"The black-scholes benchmark now always runs under MPI. Output matches the original, and pricing time scales close to linearly with rank count.\n\n**Changes** (only `black-scholes/black_scholes.cpp` and `black-scholes/CMakeLists.txt`; executable name unchanged, no new files):\n\n- **Distribution:** options are split into contiguous blocks, one per rank. Each option depends only on its global index, so each rank builds its own options and no input data is communicated.\n- **Output:** `-r` (full statistics and hash) and `-v` need the ordered results on rank 0, so results are gathered there with `MPI_Gatherv`. The gather is skipped without `-r`/`-v`, and `-v` gathers only the first 10 results.\n- **Timing:** barrier, then time the pricing loop, then report the maximum across ranks. `Computation time` and `Options per second` keep their original meaning.\n- **Output and exit codes:** only rank 0 prints, and the exit code is broadcast so all ranks agree.\n- **One addition:** a `MPI ranks: N` line after the option count. Remove it if external parsers are strict about the format.\n- **CMake:** `find_package(MPI REQUIRED)` and link `MPI::MPI_CXX`. It's unconditional, with no external dependencies beyond MPI itself.\n\n**Verification:**\n- Compared against the unmodified program across 12 argument sets (including `-n 0`, counts smaller than the rank count, and `-h`/bad-option paths) and rank counts 1 to 16. All numeric output, including sums and hashes, is identical.\n- A 2,000,003-option `-r -v` run on 7 ranks is byte-identical to the baseline apart from timing lines.\n- Pricing time for 40M options: 5.53 s on 1 rank, 2.82 s on 2, 1.39 s on 4, 0.69 s on 8, 0.37 s on 16.\n\n**Limits:**\n- With `-r`, rank 0 still hashes and summarizes the full array serially. That keeps the output identical to the original, but it becomes the bottleneck for very large `-n`.\n- `-march=native` is kept from the original. On a heterogeneous cluster, that flag may need changing.\n- I tested only with Open MPI on one node, and oversubscribed runs were very slow, so I limited the sweep to 16 ranks.","time":{"start":1793116976744,"end":1793116979970}}}
